decisions.summary: Phase 1 planned to the task; phases 2-4 to their approach, each planned to the task when it opens by a reviewed plan amendment.

decisions.summary: serde_json is the one crate phase 1 adds; further crates named per phase.
decisions.why: Implementation choice the request and spec leave open; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Every check in-process; one l7r-guard call per hook event.
decisions.why: Implements FR-007.

decisions.summary: Deciders run in today's settings order; refusals reported together, rewrites applied in order.
decisions.why: Makes the merged answer deterministic; serves FR-002's same-verdict rule.

decisions.summary: Dispatcher lands empty; each guard switches in its own commit removing its shell entry after its suite passes.

decisions.summary: A fact several deciders need is read once per process.
decisions.why: Carries FR-006's per-process design fixes.

decisions.id: D7 - binary from its own tree, failing open
decisions.summary: The wrapper builds the binary when sources are newer; a failure to build or run lets the call through with a notice and a guard-log line.
decisions.why: The request and spec say nothing on failure modes and no requirement is narrowed. Note: the justification that a crashing guard lets the call through today is stated, not measured, and one build failure now turns off all guards at once rather than one; that is design, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: pair-hooks, gate-hooks, measure-hooks, no-poll-hooks, main-tree-hooks, record-edit-hooks, then settings order.
decisions.why: Order of work inside phase 1; changes no scope.

decisions.summary: Scale/Scope states phase 1 is the 26 repository guards, their libraries and suites; the work breakdown (planned to the task) has no line for the inline Python sites in tests/hooks/ (and any non-guard Python in scripts/hooks/), keeps tests/hooks/hookdeps.py as Python rekeyed with no phase for its port, and item 7 only re-runs and records the census rather than requiring phase 1's share to return nothing.

Nothing makes those impossible in phase 1; the narrowing is unlisted rather than argued, and it would reach ticked tasks. Fix: a work-breakdown line porting phase 1's inline sites (the suites' python3 -c and heredocs) and any remaining scripts/hooks/ Python; a stated phase and FR-001 basis for hookdeps.py (ported in phase 1, or named as the gate planner's in phase 2); item 7 to require phase 1's share of both censuses to return nothing.

decisions.summary: ci/, the gate's scripts, _invocation.py, switches.py and the gate recipes' inline Python; the Rust-only route lands early since it is most of SC-002.
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase-2 list and serves SC-002.

decisions.id: P3-SCOPE - tooling list omits the Makefile's other recipes
decisions.summary: Phase 3's approach names the rest of scripts/, tools/, pipeline/, helpers, specs/, recorded measurements and .specify/scripts/bash/ but not the inline Python of the Makefile's other recipes, which phase 2 explicitly does not claim; the shell scripts under specs/ are covered only by 'every file under specs/'.
decisions.why: FR-001 assigns the Makefile's other recipes and the shell scripts under specs/ to phase 3; as written those sites sit in no phase block. Lesser consequence than P1-SCOPE: phase 3 is approach-level, will be planned to the task and reviewed again, and SC-005's close would catch it - but it should be fixed in the same amendment by naming both in phase 3's approach.

decisions.id: P3 - tests rewritten as Rust, one end-to-end kept
decisions.summary: One crate a family of tools; each tool's tests rewritten in Rust, its one end-to-end test kept.
decisions.why: Implements FR-008 and FR-001's tests-with-their-piece rule.

decisions.summary: Mode A planner, pool generators, interactive/, then containers, lockfiles, pyproject tables and __init__.py last; close on SC-005.
decisions.why: Matches FR-001's phase-4 list and SC-005.

decisions.id: Bookends - phase not closed while its criterion is unmet
decisions.summary: No make perf bookends through phase 3; each phase re-runs its m: commands and is not closed while its success criterion is unmet; phase 4 takes bookends.
decisions.why: Implements FR-010 and is stricter than it; no map is rolled before phase 4.

decisions.id: Constitution X - discipline read for Rust
decisions.summary: Clippy pedantic, rustfmt, full coverage, red-green, function and file size limits; no overlap check added; remaining Python keeps clause 10's rules.
decisions.why: Holds FR-004 and keeps today's Rust crate rules; the request asks nothing about discipline changes.

decisions.id: Constitution XIV - two guards fixed in their port
decisions.summary: The make-only guard's pytest-in-grep misread and the guard-file guard's scratch-text misread are fixed as they move, case verdict changed and named in the same commit.
decisions.why: FR-002's own named exception, with its conditions repeated.

blocks: ### T006-T049 - one task a guard (phase 1, work breakdown 5, 7)
### T050-T052 - the suites' tooling and the close (phase 1, work breakdown 6-8)

decisions.summary: Technical Context: Rust edition 2021 on the toolchain rust/phases builds with; a Cargo workspace, phase 1's crate rust/guard with binary l7r-guard; storage files only, as today
decisions.why: Unchanged from the CLEAR text apart from the crate line; the request is to make this a Rust codebase and these choices do not narrow it.

decisions.summary: fancy-regex added as the second external crate so the guards' patterns that use lookaround or backreferences can be carried over verbatim; hm_shape.py (heredoc and quote stripping) ported in T003 with it
decisions.why: A dependency choice serving FR-002 (same verdicts) and FR-001 (every Python file replaced by Rust); it narrows nothing the GM asked. The ruling does not depend on the count of 43 (research R8, 2026-11-07, not re-runnable from this bundle): one lookaround pattern would be enough to need the crate to keep the patterns verbatim. What actually holds FR-002 is the per-guard suite replay (D4) going green, not the Complexity row's premise that a verbatim pattern gives identical verdicts - Python re and fancy-regex differ at edges ($ before a trailing newline, Unicode \d/\w, \Z).

decisions.summary: A hand-written matcher in place of a fancy-regex pattern only where a profile shows that pattern hot, decided in its guard's task
decisions.why: A design default inside the request; the verdicts stay bound by FR-002 and its suite either way.

decisions.summary: serde_json for the protocol; the wrapper keeps the last good binary and fails open only when none was ever built (D7, R6)
decisions.why: Text carried from blocks judged CLEAR; unchanged in substance.

decisions.summary: Workspace root rust/Cargo.toml naming phases and guard; protocol and merge (D1, D2); shared state and facts asked once (D5, D6, T003); wrapper keeping the last good binary (T004); settings switch landed with an empty guard list, the dispatcher called once an event beside the shell guards it does not yet hold, its floor timed (T005)
decisions.why: The transitional coexistence keeps FR-003 (no guard runs twice) and works toward FR-007; nothing asked is dropped. Carried from the CLEAR range block plus the fancy-regex line judged above.

decisions.summary: One task a guard: the Rust guard registered, the shell and its settings entry removed in the same commit (D3, FR-003); the guard's suite as its verdict replay, its inline Python replaced in the same task (D4); order by measured cost first (R2); each task landed with make land-tooling
decisions.why: Applies FR-001, FR-002 and FR-003 guard by guard; the order and the landing route narrow nothing. The 44 tasks T006-T049 match the 44 registered guards in Technical Context. FR-002's 'every case its tests and its suites hold' still binds each task: the Done line names the suite, and any other test of the same guard's cases is not displaced by it.

decisions.id: T028 / T029 / T006-T049 range: XIV fixes
decisions.summary: Two constitution XIV fixes, on make-only-hooks and guard-file-hooks, taken under FR-002's exception; the template line 'XIV's fix named' on the other guard blocks
decisions.why: FR-002 itself provides this exception (a guard that refuses correct work today is fixed in its port, its expected verdict changed, the change named in the commit and the phase's record). The range block names exactly two guards; each fix's legitimacy is for its own task, where the case and the change are visible. The template line on the other 42 blocks grants no further license, since FR-002 already conditions the exception on the guard refusing correct work today. T028/T029 say 'named in its task'; FR-002's 'named in the commit and in the phase's record' still binds and the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: The four tests/hooks Python helpers (hookbench, hookdeps, hooktrace, test_hooks_cases) ported as l7r-guard subcommands and crate tests; done when no .py remains under tests/hooks/
decisions.why: FR-001 puts each tests/ file with the piece it tests; FR-008 applies. The Done line is narrower than FR-001's recorded-measurement clause, which binds this commit: every specs/*/measurements*.json command that runs one of these helpers (m:hooks-bash and m:pair-hooks-suite, which T052 re-runs, plausibly among them) is rewritten in the commit that ports it and re-run as its proof. The clause still binds; the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: Each guard library deleted with its last caller; done when no .py and no inline Python remain under scripts/hooks/, make audit and make guard-log reading the Rust lines unchanged
decisions.why: Porting a library nothing calls would be unrequested scope; deleting it with its last caller completes FR-001 for phase 1. As with T050, FR-001's recorded-measurement rewrite binds the commits that port or delete these files (T003 included); the Done line does not displace it.

decisions.summary: Phase 1 closed: figures re-run and recorded beside their first values, SC-001 met, both censuses' phase-1 share empty
decisions.why: FR-010 (timings measured against the spec's figures) and FR-001 (both censuses re-run at the phase's end) applied to phase 1; SC-002 and SC-003 belong to later phases and the feature's close. FR-010's 'recorded in dev/' and FR-002's 'named in the phase's record' for the two XIV fixes still bind this close; the Done line does not displace them.

decisions.summary: With no good binary ever built, the wrapper lets the call through with a notice and a guard-log line
decisions.why: This is plan D7's own outcome, not new in this block. It is held against FR-002, which asks for the same verdicts on every case the tests and suites hold. Having no binary at all is not one of those cases. The case that matches it today is a guard whose Python cannot start, and m:python-dead-fails-open measures that this already fails open (repo-safety exits 0 on a force push to main, make-only prints nothing, gate exits 127). So no verdict gets weaker than today's. Making it fail closed would be new behavior the GM did not ask for. The earlier BLOCKED version justified this from FR-005's make-only clause. The block now cites the requirement that actually governs verdicts.

decisions.summary: A failed build (does not compile, or compiles and fails l7r-guard --self-check) runs the last good binary; a stale build is rebuilt
decisions.why: This repeats D7 word for word, and the self-check is D7's own definition of a good build. Today a broken Python guard crashes and fails open, so keeping the previous guards running gives a verdict no weaker than today's. The request asks for a port and nothing here cuts what it covers.

decisions.summary: T004 replaces no guard; T005 adds the wrapper to the settings with an empty guard list; each guard task moves one decider in and removes that guard's shell script and settings entry in the same landing
decisions.why: This is how the plan carries out FR-003: the Python stays the one that runs until its replacement passes, and no piece runs in both. Separate processes for the guards still being moved are a temporary state. FR-007's one process is where the work ends up, and this order does not give it up.

decisions.summary: FR-005's clause that the make-only guard must cover the replacements' binaries is left to T028, not this task
decisions.why: This assigns the requirement to another task and narrows nothing. The clause is about the make-only guard's coverage, not about the wrapper. FR-005 still applies to the feature in full, and the block names the task that carries it.

decisions.summary: No work budget, nothing rolled, for a tooling landing.

decisions.summary: With no good binary ever built, the wrapper lets the call through with a notice and a guard-log line
decisions.why: This is plan D7's own outcome, not new in this block. It is held against FR-002, which asks for the same verdicts on every case the tests and suites hold. Having no binary at all is not one of those cases. The case that matches it today is a guard whose Python cannot start, and m:python-dead-fails-open measures that this already fails open (repo-safety exits 0 on a force push to main, make-only prints nothing, gate exits 127). So no verdict gets weaker than today's. Making it fail closed would be new behavior the GM did not ask for. The earlier BLOCKED version justified this from FR-005's make-only clause. The block now cites the requirement that actually governs verdicts.

decisions.summary: A failed build (does not compile, or compiles and fails l7r-guard --self-check) runs the last good binary; a stale build is rebuilt
decisions.why: This repeats D7 word for word, and the self-check is D7's own definition of a good build. Today a broken Python guard crashes and fails open, so keeping the previous guards running gives a verdict no weaker than today's. The request asks for a port and nothing here cuts what it covers.

decisions.summary: T004 replaces no guard; T005 adds the wrapper to the settings with an empty guard list; each guard task moves one decider in and removes that guard's shell script and settings entry in the same landing
decisions.why: This is how the plan carries out FR-003: the Python stays the one that runs until its replacement passes, and no piece runs in both. Separate processes for the guards still being moved are a temporary state. FR-007's one process is where the work ends up, and this order does not give it up.

decisions.summary: FR-005's clause that the make-only guard must cover the replacements' binaries is left to T028, not this task
decisions.why: This assigns the requirement to another task and narrows nothing. The clause is about the make-only guard's coverage, not about the wrapper. FR-005 still applies to the feature in full, and the block names the task that carries it.

decisions.summary: Lands through make land-tooling with no work budget and nothing rolled; no researched value or constant moves
decisions.why: This is process and tooling scope only. Nothing the GM asked for is changed.

decisions.summary: Every session's settings call the one dispatcher once per event, beside the Python guards it does not yet hold.
decisions.why: FR-001 ports the hooks first and FR-003 requires each unported guard's Python to stay the one that runs while no guard runs twice; FR-007's single process is the end state reached as pieces move in. A coexistence period is what FR-003 itself describes, not a carve-out from the GM's request to make this a Rust codebase.

decisions.summary: After T004; landed alone with make land-tooling.
decisions.why: Sequencing and landing route only; the spec leaves both open and neither narrows what is ported.

decisions.summary: Green: settings call it for every event, make hooks-test green, its floor timed. Red: failure recorded, task set down, process stop to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The green exit enforces FR-002/FR-003 (hooks-test) and FR-010 (timed); the red exit stops rather than relaxing any requirement.

decisions.summary: No work budget, nothing rolled, for a tooling landing.
decisions.why: Process bookkeeping; it changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: Re-run m:hooks-bash's command with the dispatcher in place and record the floor.
decisions.why: Serves FR-010 and SC-001's measurement against m:hooks-bash; it does not claim SC-001 met or move its target.

decisions.id: T005-6 no constant or room question
decisions.summary: No researched value moves; no constant moved; not a room question.
decisions.why: Statements that the task touches only Claude Code tool-call guards, consistent with FR-009's scope and the request.

decisions.summary: Guard by guard with shell and settings entry removed in the registering commit (D3/FR-003); suite as verdict replay with its inline Python replaced in the same task (D4); order by measured cost first (R2); the two XIV fixes on make-only-hooks and guard-file-hooks (FR-002's exception).
decisions.why: Each is settled by the accepted spec (D3, D4, FR-002's named exception, FR-003) and none is T006's own: the XIV fixes belong to two other guards' tasks, so T006 changes no expected verdict. Putting pair-hooks first agrees with m:hooks-bash, which names it the slowest guard.

decisions.summary: The Rust decider keeps consulting the eight phase-3 Python tools (checkpoint.py, plan_gate.py, review_prereq.py, review_owed.py, gate-stamp.py, make engine-key, hm_arbiter.py, hm_dropped.py) by path on its two rare branches and at Stop, until each tool's own port answers in-process.
decisions.why: FR-001 fixes the phase order (hooks first, tooling in phase 3) and FR-003 requires a piece's Python to stay the one that runs until its replacement passes, so a hook ported in phase 1 has to call the tooling that is still Python. FR-007 asks for one guard process per tool call, not one per guard. It does not forbid the guard calling external tools, and the plain Bash path that SC-001/m:hooks-bash measures reaches none of them. This is temporary sequencing the spec requires, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: The engine key (a find over l7r/ and pool/, plus make engine-key when the cache is stale) is computed only on the two branches that read it, not on every call.
decisions.why: Removing work that changes no verdict serves the request's purpose (the GM: the Python code is too inefficient), and FR-002's suite replay gates it. Two notes that are not rulings: (1) the citation is stretched, because FR-006 names three specific fixes and the plan's paraphrase 'a fact computed once, and only where it is used' is broader than the text; (2) today every call has a side effect, refreshing the cached key, and the claim that 'no other branch reads it' is shown only by the suite. If anything outside pair-hooks reads that cache and relies on the per-call refresh, FR-002's 'outputs' would cover it. Whether anything does was not measured in this bundle.

decisions.summary: The guard's inline Python state handling (pairing state, review rounds, dispatch record, bypass log, read_field) becomes Rust over the same files and formats.
decisions.why: This is the port FR-001 asks for, and keeping the same files and formats is what FR-002's same-outputs rule requires.

decisions.summary: The suite's "$HOOK" pretool|stop runs l7r-guard --only pair-hooks PreToolUse|Stop through a shared shim tests/hooks/guard-shim.sh, with the suite's cases unchanged.
decisions.why: This is D4 as written: the suite points at l7r-guard --only <guard> and its cases are unchanged. The shim only maps the suite's existing argument form onto the binary's.

decisions.summary: Green: the suite passes against the Rust guard, plus rust-test, cover and hooks-test. Red: record the failure and stop to make arbiter-ask. Landed by make land-tooling with no work budget.
decisions.why: The exits restate FR-002/FR-003/FR-004's gates, and the landing route is process that narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: hm_make.py's targets, combine and classify-through-bare-pytest move to rust/guard/src/shared/make.rs with gate-hooks, patterns verbatim; the rest of hm_make.py moves with make-only-hooks (T028) and guard-file-hooks (T029).
decisions.why: Partitions a shared library across the guards that read it; every part is still ported (FR-001, the request's 'all be ported to Rust'), verbatim patterns keep FR-002's same verdicts, and the suite replay (D4) checks the result. Nothing is left in Python that the request or spec would have ported.

decisions.summary: The decider reads tool_input.command as JSON instead of the shell's greedy sed, so a ' -k ' in the description field no longer arms the subset flag; a suite case is added, the fix named in the commit and the phase's record.
decisions.why: Applies the one exception the accepted FR-002 already states - a guard refusing correct work (a later make done refused on a falsely armed subset flag) is fixed in its port under constitution XIV - with that exception's conditions met: the case lands in the same commit and the change is named in the commit and the phase's record. It narrows nothing the GM asked for; the request is to make the codebase Rust, not to preserve a misparse.

decisions.summary: gate-hooks.sh's status mode is ported: l7r-guard --only gate-hooks status prints the same subset_pending= line, reached through the shim's status mode.
decisions.why: Preserves an existing output as FR-002 requires (same verdicts and outputs); it reverses the dropping the earlier preflight ruled NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: After T005, independent of the other guards; green exit is the suite against l7r-guard --only gate-hooks plus rust-test, cover and hooks-test; the shell and its settings entry go in the commit that registers the decider.
decisions.why: Restates D3 (guard by guard, never both, FR-003) and D4 (the suite is the replay), and FR-004's coverage floor; no new scope.

decisions.summary: The sanitized command and the last full gate are read in-process; gatecost.py (asked only on a streak's first expensive measurement, for its reminder's median) stays the measure tool's, asked by path, until phase 3 ports it.
decisions.why: FR-001 orders the port in four phases and FR-003 keeps a piece's Python the one that runs until its replacement passes; gatecost.py belongs to a later phase, so calling it where the shell did is what those require, not a carve-out from them. It is not a guard, so FR-007's one process per tool call is not touched. Nothing the guard decides is left out of the port.

decisions.summary: The shell's greedy read (from the payload's last "command" key to its last quote) is kept for the git commit reset only, reproduced over the input in its own key order.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires the same verdicts as the shell on every suite case, and its only exception (XIV) is for a guard that refuses correct work. A later field naming git commit RESETS the streak, which makes the guard more permissive, so it refuses nothing correct, and the exception does not reach it. Keeping the shell's behavior is FR-002 applied as written. Reproducing the span over the re-serialized input rather than the raw bytes is a design choice; FR-002 judges it on the suite's cases, which the exits require to pass.

decisions.summary: status is ported, printing the same measurements_since_reset=N budget=B line.
decisions.why: FR-002: same outputs as the piece replaced.

decisions.summary: The shell guard and its settings entry are removed in the commit that registers the Rust decider, after test-measure-hooks.sh passes against l7r-guard --only measure-hooks.
decisions.why: Plan D3/D4 and FR-003 (never both), stated as accepted.

decisions.summary: hm_shape.py's wait/sleep/watch/self-matching/ceiling/periodic-report functions move to rust/guard/src/shared/wait.rs with each pattern verbatim; the rest of hm_shape.py (executing_backticks) moves with the guard that reads it
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every tracked Python file and D3 moves guards one by one; porting the library the guard reads, patterns verbatim, is how FR-002's same-verdicts requirement is met. Nothing is left in Python or dropped - the remainder is assigned to its own guard's port.

decisions.summary: the periodic-report refusal's cron minute stays the local minute, read via `date +%M` only on the backgrounded-periodic-report branch
decisions.why: Keeps the Python's verdict and output (time.localtime().tm_min) exactly, which is what FR-002 requires; the earlier UTC alternative was the deviation and is already rejected. A child process on one rare branch is a mechanism choice, not a second guard process (FR-007 is about one process per tool call for the guards), and it changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: self_matching compiles the command's pgrep -f pattern with fancy-regex instead of Python re, skips a pattern it cannot compile as the Python skipped one re could not, and rests dialect-divergence detection on the suite replay
decisions.why: FR-002 scopes equivalence to every case the tests and suites hold, and D4 makes the suite the replay; the decision meets that bound, preserves the skip-on-uncompilable behavior, and states plainly that divergence outside the suite is not covered - which is the spec's own bound, not a carve-out from it. A Rust port cannot use Python's re, so a different engine is inherent to the request.

decisions.summary: The verdict library scripts/hooks/lib/hm_tree.py (judge, explain, log context) is ported whole, each pattern verbatim, to rust/guard/src/shared/tree.rs, shared with gm-tree-hooks, which moves to it in its own task.
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every Python file and FR-002 asks for the same verdicts; porting the library the verdict comes from, verbatim, is how the guard is ported. Done-measured deletes only main-tree-hooks.sh and its settings entry, so hm_tree.py stays for gm-tree-hooks until that guard's own replacement passes (FR-003, D3).

decisions.summary: The session's clone comes from T003's session facts through the same resolver ported (claim map, last /rename, sessions json), not from spawning clone-sync-hooks.sh resolve.
decisions.why: The same resolution with the same inputs, run in the one guard process FR-007 requires; FR-002's suite replay (D4) checks the verdicts.

decisions.summary: The mirror root comes from walking up to the nearest .git (T006's find_root) and cutting at /.clones/, not from git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
decisions.why: A mechanism change stated to give the same answer, which the suite replay must confirm before the switch (FR-002, D4). It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The refusal and the rewrite's context name rust/guard/src/guards/main_tree_hooks.rs instead of scripts/hooks/main-tree-hooks.sh, which this task deletes; no verdict changes.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-002's 'same outputs', and the only exception FR-002 names is the XIV fix, so it is judged as a carve-out. Applied literally, the rule would make the guard send a refused session to a file this same commit deletes. That defeats what the message is for, which is telling the reader where the rule lives. It does not reach what FR-002 is for, proving the port changes no decision, because only the self-referencing path changes and every verdict and all other text stay as they are. The precedent is T006. If a suite case asserts the path, its expected text changes in the same commit and the commit must name that change.

decisions.summary: The hook half of scripts/measure/event_log.py (line, verdict reading, categories, log path, append) moves into the Rust decider with patterns, fields and order verbatim; the from-transcript command stays Python until phase 3 ports the measure tools.
decisions.why: The request is to make the codebase Rust; FR-001 orders the port in phases with the hooks first. The code that runs on every hook event is the hook's, and porting it with the guard is the hooks phase doing its job. The part that is a command, not a hook, goes in the later measure-tools phase, which FR-001's phase order already provides; nothing is excluded from the port. Keeping the line's fields and order the same is what FR-002 requires so that feature-report reads it unchanged.

decisions.summary: On an Edit, the reversal test (hm_arbiter.reversal) runs in-process in Rust; recording the trip is handed to hm_arbiter.py by path, and only when a reversal is found, until the arbiter is ported.
decisions.why: The arbiter is its own piece in FR-001's phase order, and this block does not port it. Calling it by path, and only on the rare reversal, keeps Python off the common path, which is the hook start-up cost the GM's request was about, and it lasts only until the arbiter's own port, so no Python is kept for good. FR-003 is per piece: the guard's verdict comes from Rust alone, so no piece runs both. The block follows T006 (a).

decisions.summary: The log line's ev is taken from the payload's hook_event_name, as the Python did; l7r-guard --only with no event name reads it from the payload, so the suite's "$HOOK" replays unchanged.
decisions.why: This keeps the Python's behavior (FR-002) and lets the guard's existing suite replay against the Rust guard without edits (D4). It is an interface detail that serves the spec and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The edit digest stays SHA-1's first 12 hex digits, written as a small SHA-1 in shared beside T006's SHA-256 rather than taken from a crate.
decisions.why: Keeping the digest format is FR-002 (same outputs). Writing the hash in shared rather than using a crate is a design choice, not a fidelity question, and it narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The tools the guard asks (git, sync-with-main.sh, own-make.sh, gate_lock.py, clone_local_settings.py, solo.py, usage_log.py, layout_carry.sh) stay theirs and are asked by path until their own ports.
decisions.why: The request ports all the Python and the spec phases it (FR-001); FR-003 requires the Python to remain the one that runs until its replacement passes. Each tool is named as ending at its own port, so this is order, not an exclusion.

decisions.summary: The session facts the guard's inline Python read (input fields, canonical clone, whether another claimant is live) are read in-process from T003's facts and /proc; the notice's make targets use shared::make::targets.
decisions.why: This is the port itself, what the request asks for; the block binds it to the same answers, which is FR-002.

decisions.summary: The script stays as its resolve mode only, code unchanged and outside l7r-guard, until T051 deletes its callers; prompt and pretool leave in this task.
decisions.why: Sequencing, not a carve-out: (1) the kept code has a named remover, T051, so nothing is excluded from the port the request asks for and FR-001 phases; (2) the guard runs on one path, since resolve is not a guard mode and both guard modes and both settings entries go in the commit that registers the decider (item 9, D3), so FR-003 is met; (3) FR-002 is untouched, the resolve code being unchanged. The not-through-l7r-guard reasoning (recursion, cargo build) is mechanism and decides nothing here either way. Two points for the record: step 1 says 'its shell gone' while (c) keeps the script, and item 9 is the operative statement; and (b) ports the canonical-clone lookup while (c) keeps the shell's canonical_clone for the other guards, so two implementations are live until T051. That is not FR-003's 'both', each call taking one path, but T051 owes the deletion of the shell's version as well as of its callers.

decisions.summary: The prompt mode's lines are the decider's plain-stdout answer, byte for byte, so the suite's prompt cases pass unedited.
decisions.why: Directly FR-002: same outputs, suite expectations unedited.

decisions.summary: Every mode (stop, prompt, timer, stagger) moves to Rust; the detached wait and printed stagger become the binary's --idle-tests entry, started by setsid nohup as the shell was; the GM's disable of 2026-09-06 carries over as one constant, arming off.
decisions.why: Porting every mode is what the GM's 'making this a Rust codebase' and D3 ask, and leaves no shell behind. Keeping arming off is FR-002 (same verdicts), not a carve-out. FR-007's one process concerns the guards deciding a tool call, not a background wait started the way the shell started it.

decisions.summary: git, setsid, nohup, kill, pgrep and the run itself stay external tools asked by path; the lock is the flock tool on the lock file's descriptor.
decisions.why: These are system tools, not Python or shell in the repository, so FR-001 is untouched and nothing the GM asked for is reduced. The stated semantics (a lock owned by the open file the timer holds, as fd 9 was) keep FR-002. The choice of flock tool over a library call is design, which this mode does not grade.

decisions.summary: The small tools and the Python fragments go in-process (field, state_of, JSON, cksum with the same CRC values, ls -t, clone top); the JSON's keys and values are the same, its key order and indentation are not held.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds outputs 'on every case its tests and its suites hold'. Key order and indentation are outside that unless a case holds them, and if one does the block's own exit (every case of the suite passes, expectations unedited but the one in d-2) fails and the task is set down, so the obligation is not reduced. The request says nothing of byte layout. The premise that each reader takes it by key could not be checked from the bundle; the exit, not the premise, is what keeps this within.

decisions.summary: $HOOK stagger <name> reaches --idle-tests through the shim.
decisions.why: D4 points HOOK at the Rust guard; the shim routes the case's unchanged input to the entry of (a). No expectation moves.

decisions.summary: The case 'the shipped default IS disabled' grepped the shell's DEF_ARM=0; it reads the Rust constant instead.
decisions.why: This edits a case of the suite D4 makes the replay and FR-002 holds, so it is ruled on, not passed as within. The general rule is physically impossible here: the case greps a file the port must delete (D3, the GM's move to Rust), so it cannot pass unedited once the shell is gone. The case's purpose survives whole: it pins the GM's disable where that disable now lives, and its expected result is unchanged, so this is not FR-002's verdict-change exception and needs no XIV fix. It covers this one case; the block states every other expectation is unedited.

decisions.summary: Every mode of agent-stall-hooks is ported: prompt becomes the guard; check, watch, pending and ack become the binary's --agent-stall, with the Python scan done in-process and one read of each transcript's last line.
decisions.why: A complete port, which is what the request and FR-001 ask, with FR-002's same outputs. Read as: the scan the embedded Python did is now Rust code inside the Rust process. If it instead meant the binary still runs Python, it would contradict the request and FR-001; the block's goal and its 'script's logic gone' support the port reading, and the repository was not opened to confirm it.

decisions.summary: scripts/hooks/agent-stall-hooks.sh stays until T051 as a forwarder holding only a call to l7r-guard.sh --agent-stall, because this guard's report and engine-freeze-hooks' refusal print that path and sessions run watch by hand; its hook mode leaves the settings in this task (with item 9, the done-condition).
decisions.why: Does not narrow what was asked. The request and FR-001 replace Python with Rust; the forwarder is one line of shell and no Python runs. FR-003: the forwarder runs only Rust, so no piece runs both. D3 requires the settings entry to leave in the decider's commit, which the block does, and says nothing of deleting the file. FR-002: the printed command is an output, and keeping the path keeps it true. Removal at T051 is sequencing, not scope; T051's content is outside this bundle and was not checked. FR-005 (make the one entry point) is not cited by the block, but this is a hand-run path sessions already use, not a new one. Item 1's 'its shell gone' is looser than item 9, which states the actual condition; a wording tension in the plan, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: watch still loops until killed; a tick count from the environment ends it for a unit test; the seams AGENT_STALE_S, AGENT_RECENT_S and AGENT_TICK_S are kept.
decisions.why: The tick count exists only so a test of an endless loop can meet FR-008; with FR-008 gone it has no purpose. watch's behavior is unchanged when it is unset, and keeping the existing seams serves FR-002 and D4.

decisions.summary: Ordering: after T005, in the plan's order, independent of the other guards.
decisions.why: D3's guard-by-guard order after the dispatcher lands; FR-001 puts the hooks first.

decisions.summary: Exits: the guard's suite green against l7r-guard --only agent-stall-hooks, make rust-test and cover green, make hooks-test green; on red, record and stop to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: D4's replay as the switch condition, FR-002 and FR-003, and FR-004's coverage floor. The red exit is process and changes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Lands by make land-tooling with no work budget, nothing rolled.
decisions.why: Landing mechanics for tooling; it does not touch any requirement or the request.

decisions.summary: lib/stall_watchdog.py (the pass) is ported to stall_watchdog_hooks/pass.rs with the shell; prompt is the guard, run and once are the binary's --stall-watchdog
decisions.why: FR-001 puts scripts/hooks/ and the libraries its guards call in phase 1, and the GM asked for all the Python to be ported. This resolves round 1's BLOCKED on keeping the file in Python. Item 9's measured Done names the shell and settings entry but not the .py; that is an omission and not a decision to keep it, since (a) states the port and FR-001's phase-end census refuses a survivor.

decisions.summary: Each loop pass still starts a fresh process through the wrapper, so an update to what a stall is reaches a running loop
decisions.why: Keeps the existing behavior under FR-002. The block does not name the wrapper; items 1 and 9 (shell and settings entry gone) constrain it to the Rust binary's entry, and nothing in the text retains the Python.

decisions.summary: The Rust loop still asks finished-run-hooks.sh live by path until T017 moves it
decisions.why: D3 moves guards one per commit, so a mixed interim is the approved order. FR-003 is per piece: this piece has one runner and the other guard has one runner. The dependency is named and bounded by T017.

decisions.summary: kill -0 becomes the /proc/<pid> check; the one-instance lock is T014's flock moved to shared::tool, its descriptor closed for children by default; the sleep is in-process
decisions.why: Implementation choices inside a port. FR-002's equality is enforced by the exit that every suite case passes against the Rust guard.

decisions.summary: The guard does nothing when L7R_SELF_CHECK is set, which main.rs's self-check sandbox sets
decisions.why: The one except-when in the section, adjudicated as such. FR-002's domain is every case the tests and suites hold; --self-check is a harness of the Rust build that the block says the shell never faced, and the variable is set by that sandbox alone, so no suite case or real prompt reaches the branch. It removes no behavior the GM or the spec asked for. The exit requires every suite case green against the Rust guard without that variable.

decisions.summary: The loop ends if its state directory disappears, so a loop started under a suite's moved HOME does not run for ever
decisions.why: An added end condition on a directory-less loop, not a verdict or an output of any case FR-002 covers; if the suite held a contrary case, the exit would fail. It does not touch what the watchdog is for: the block states the real state directory is never removed, and the guard on the prompt path is what starts the loop.

decisions.summary: A count of passes from the environment ends run for a unit test, as T015's (c); STALL_PERIOD and STALL_STATE_DIR kept
decisions.why: A test seam that serves FR-008 and adds no behavior outside the tests; the two existing variables are retained under FR-002.

decisions.summary: Sequence after T005, independent of the other guards; exits are the guard's suite against l7r-guard --only, make rust-test, cover and make hooks-test; shell and settings entry gone in the commit that registers the decider; landed by make land-tooling
decisions.why: D3 and D4 as the spec states them, with FR-004's coverage floor carried by cover.

decisions.id: (a) every mode and all its Python ported
decisions.summary: prompt and stop become the guard; check, seen, live, judge and stale become the binary's --finished-run; the inline Python moves in-process with its rules unchanged.
decisions.why: This is the whole of the piece, nothing left in Python: the GM's 'all be ported to Rust', FR-001 and FR-002.

decisions.id: (a)-proc every process fact from /proc, never a pattern over the hook's own command line
decisions.summary: How process facts are read in the port.
decisions.why: An implementation means, stated under 'rules unchanged'. FR-002 binds its verdicts on every suite case, and D4's replay in exit 6 settles that by run; if a verdict moved, FR-002's XIV path would have to name it, and the block claims none.

decisions.id: (a)-T016 the watchdog pass asks live in-process
decisions.summary: T016's landed watchdog stops calling the script and calls the port directly.
decisions.why: A direct consequence of the port and of FR-003: the caller reaches the one implementation. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.id: (b) the script stays as a forwarder until T051
decisions.summary: finished-run-hooks.sh remains only to run l7r-guard.sh --finished-run for review_prereq.py (phase 3); its hook modes leave the settings in this task.
decisions.why: Sequencing, not a carve-out. The request and FR-001 are about Python; the forwarder holds no Python and no logic, and has a named end at T051. FR-003 holds: only the Rust runs, the forwarder decides nothing. D3 asks that the shell entry leave the settings in the decider's commit, which this does. The premise that review_prereq.py is the only caller does not decide the ruling: the forwarder answers any caller of that path.

decisions.id: (c) the tools it asks stay theirs: lib/writer-alive.sh asked by path until T051
decisions.summary: The port keeps shelling out to the shell helper for each waiter's file.
decisions.why: The helper is described as shell, not Python, so FR-001 does not reach it, and it has a named end at T051. FR-007 (not cited by the block, its first line read in spec-index.md) is one process per GUARD rather than per helper, and finished-run-hooks' guard modes are prompt and stop rather than the before-Bash path SC-001 measures. Premise on record: the block does not say on which modes the helper runs, and within rests on the helper holding no inline Python.

decisions.id: (d)-1 os.access(path, X_OK) restated as the file's execute bits
